tasks.title: Task 1A
tasks.statement: Walk from the start point S1 near the Golf restaurant to the Stop S2 at the Amphitheater on the eastern part of Pioneer City. On your way, identify all of the following features, located within the zone, circled on Map 1A by a RED LINE: open air sports facilities, children playgrounds, buildings. On Map 1A, identify and label with numbers the features which are already mapped. You will also see features which are not indicated on the map. Draw and label those features on the map, ensuring you label each with a number. Use only a pen (blue, black, or other color, if needed)! Write down the numbers of all these features in the table on the response sheet and provide the following data for them: For all open air features, including sports facilities, report the purpose of use and estimate the maximum number of users (players, watchers, visitors) at noon (12:00) on a weekend summer sunny day. For buildings, report the condition (quality). At the Stop S2 you will have 10 minutes to complete Map 1A and Response sheet before handing them in to the Jury.

parts.question: Identify features on Map 1A and fill in the response sheet with purpose, condition (for buildings), and capacity (for open-air facilities).

tasks.title: Task 1B
tasks.statement: Walk from Stop S2 at the Amphitheater on the eastern part of Pioneer City to Stop S3. On your way, identify the geomorphologic features, located at the nine places marked by WHITE CIRCLES (Exercise Points) on Map 1B. Label each white circle with a number, corresponding to one of the geomorphologic features from the list, found on the same sheet.

parts.question: Analyze the geological profile from Košutnjak hill to Zemun (Figure 1). Identify which rock types from the list form layers annotated with capital letters on the profile. Write your answers in Table 1.

Select from the list the kinds of relief surfaces that correspond to the numbers on the profile, and enter their numbers in Table 2. Arrange them in descending order of age (from oldest to the most recent one).

In which area marked by a RED SQUARE on the map (figure 2), can you most probably find geomorphologic features, similar to those typical for the Košutnjak park? Provide your answer with the geographic coordinates of the approximate centre of this box, to the closest whole degree. What is the common name of this type of relief (terrain)?

tasks.title: Task 1C
tasks.statement: You are now at the Stop S4. Use your position as an observation point over Belgrade. Remember this panoramic view for tomorrow’s exercise (FWE-2). Complete the following tasks.

parts.question: Winter sports are gaining popularity in Belgrade. Using the data from the Košutnjak meteorological station (44°46´N 20°25´E; altitude 230 m), suggest which months will be able to support skiing season here.
You are standing near the upper point of a mountain ski run. Using Map 1C, calculate the inclination of this slope (degree, or percent).

Imagine, that you are asked to plan an open-air ice skating rink to be placed at the Pioneer City close to the running pad. Assuming that the rink is a circle with a diameter of 75 m, find an appropriate place for this rink on Map 2C, and encircle it with a pen. As the skating rink should be flat, with no relative elevation, estimate the volume of ground to be removed.

tasks.title: Fieldwork Exercise 2 - Demography
tasks.statement: All tasks must be completed individually, using the answer templates provided. The Resource Booklet contains important supporting materials: tables with statistical data, maps, etc.

parts.question: Using the demographic data and map (see Table 1 and Map 5 in the Resource Booklet), calculate the total number of potential visitors to the Košutnjak Park from the municipalities, highlighted on the Map 5, who are aged 15—25 years old in 2017.

Assuming that only one out of 1,000 (one thousand) people aged 15—25 years old from each of the countries sharing borders with Serbia, will visit Košutnjak Park this year, which country can potentially provide the largest number of young tourists?

tasks.title: Fieldwork Exercise 2 - Transportation and Accessibility
tasks.statement: Examine current transport schemes and plans for Belgrade to answer the transportation and accessibility questions.

parts.question: Examine the current (present day) public transport scheme of Belgrade (Map 6 of the Resource booklet). Which municipality highlighted on Map 5 has the easiest (fastest) connection with Pioneer City? Which municipality has the most complicated (slowest) connection with the Košutnjak Park?

There is a plan to build a tunnel for cars in Belgrade from A to B (Map 4). Provide positive justifications (benefits) for building this tunnel for future development of tourism in Košutnjak Park. Propose the shortest way to connect the Aleksandar restaurant at Košutnjak Park with the exit from the proposed tunnel (B on Map 4). Name this kind of public transport and estimate the length of its route from the tunnel exit to S4.

tasks.title: Fieldwork Exercise 2 - Human Impact (Anthropogenic Pressure)
tasks.statement: Evaluate human impact and anthropogenic pressure on the Košutnjak Park territory.

parts.question: On the Map Template 1, divide the territory of the Košutnjak Park into no more than 5 zones based on the degree of human impact (anthropogenic pressure). In the legend (key), write brief annotations for the characteristics of each zone. Briefly describe the zones and the criteria behind their allocation.

Which of the zones you have identified is characterized by the highest degree of human impact (anthropogenic pressure) on its territory? Provide a quantitative indicator to measure human impact, and estimate its average value for this zone.

tasks.title: Fieldwork Exercise 2 - Potential and limitations for sustainable development of youth tourism
tasks.statement: Analyze potential and limitations for sustainable development of youth tourism at Košutnjak Park.

parts.question: Using the Resource Booklet materials and your field observations, think about kinds of youth tourism that could be practiced here. Provide answers for: A) Which one of the already existing activities would you recommend to support and develop as a preference? B) Which one of the already existing activities would you recommend to limit? C) Which one completely new activity would you recommend for development?

Imagine, that you are designing a plan for sustainable development of youth tourism in Košutnjak Park. Link ideas for your plan to different scales (levels). For each scale, indicate the main advantages/potentials, and main limitations/constraints.
